screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows an AC source connected to one electromagnetic component — a resistor, inductor, or capacitor — a rotating phasor diagram with the angle between voltage and current marked, and an oscilloscope plotting both against a shared time axis.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for the component type, its value, the source voltage and frequency, playback, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a component and explore how its phasor relates to the AC drive, and how the part itself responds.

currentDetails.resistor: A resistor is connected. Its current is in phase with the source voltage.
currentDetails.inductor: An inductor is connected. Its current lags the source voltage by 90 degrees.
currentDetails.capacitor: A capacitor is connected. Its current leads the source voltage by 90 degrees.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a series RLC circuit driven by an AC source, a rotating voltage phasor diagram in which the resistor, inductor, and capacitor phasors close back onto the source phasor, the matching impedance triangle, and an oscilloscope plotting the source voltage and the current.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for R, L, and C, the source voltage and frequency, a checkbox to draw the phasors tip to tail, playback, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Adjust R, L, and C to see how the series impedance and voltage triangle change, and lower the frequency to find resonance.

currentDetails.inductive: The circuit is inductive: the source voltage leads the current, so the net reactance points up.
currentDetails.capacitive: The circuit is capacitive: the source voltage lags the current, so the net reactance points down.
currentDetails.resonant: The circuit is at resonance: the inductive and capacitive voltages cancel and the current is in phase with the source voltage.

controls.tipToTail: Draw the voltage phasors tip to tail

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows how the series RLC circuit responds across the whole range of driving frequencies: a current-versus-frequency curve with its resonant peak and half-power band marked, a phase-versus-frequency curve below it, and the impedance triangle, which flattens onto the resistance axis at resonance.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for R, L, and C, the source voltage and frequency, a button that sweeps the frequency across the range, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Sweep the driving frequency to find resonance, where the reactances cancel and the phase angle goes to zero, then change R to see the peak sharpen or broaden.

currentDetails.below: The drive frequency is below resonance. The circuit is capacitive, the current leads the source voltage, and the operating point is on the low-frequency side of the peak.
currentDetails.above: The drive frequency is above resonance. The circuit is inductive, the current lags the source voltage, and the operating point is on the high-frequency side of the peak.
currentDetails.at: The drive frequency is at resonance. The reactances cancel, the impedance is just the resistance, and the current is at its maximum.

controls.sweep: Sweep the source frequency across its range

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a series RLC circuit, an oscilloscope with the source voltage and the current, and below it the instantaneous power p equals v times i, shaded where energy flows into the circuit and where it flows back out, with a dashed line at the average. Beside them the power triangle relates real, reactive, and apparent power.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for R, L, and C, the source voltage and frequency, playback, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the load and watch the power factor: a resistive circuit never returns energy, while a purely reactive one consumes none at all.

currentDetails.unity: The power factor is close to one. The circuit is essentially resistive, so almost all the apparent power does work and the instantaneous power barely dips below zero.
currentDetails.lagging: The power factor is lagging: the circuit is inductive, the current lags the source voltage, and energy is handed back to the source during part of every cycle.
currentDetails.leading: The power factor is leading: the circuit is capacitive, the current leads the source voltage, and energy is handed back to the source during part of every cycle.
